title: Responses tool conversion can emit invalid function tools from chat-shaped specs
reasoning: The Responses path passes request tools directly into build_openai_responses_params, which ultimately calls build_openai_responses_tools. That converter emits Responses function tools from top-level tool.get('name'), tool.get('description'), and tool.get('parameters'). OpenAI/LiteLLM chat tool specs are commonly shaped as {'type':'function','function':{name,description,parameters}}, and this provider's non-Responses path explicitly handles that nested shape through make_openai_chat_tools_compatible. If the same chat-shaped tools reach the Responses runtime, the emitted function tool can have name=None, description=None, and default empty parameters, causing OpenAI request rejection or loss of the actual callable schema.
recommendation: Normalize both flat Windie tool specs and OpenAI chat-shaped function specs before emitting Responses tools. Extract name, description, parameters, and strict from tool['function'] when present, and add a focused unit test for chat-shaped tools in the Responses path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the excerpt shows no assertion that Responses tool conversion preserves nested chat function metadata.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that passes [{'type':'function','function':{'name':'click','description':'Click','parameters':{'type':'object','properties':{'x':{'type':'integer'}}}}}] into build_openai_responses_tools and asserts the output function has name 'click' and the original parameters.
